title: Maintaining Top-10 Suggestion Invariants in a Swift Trie for Typeahead Search
topic: Design Typeahead Search Step by Step: Why the Trie Stores the Top 10 at Every Node
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Typeahead search systems rely on rapid retrieval of the most relevant completions for a given prefix. We study a trie variant that stores, at every node, the top-10 suggestions ranked by a user-defined weight. The design preserves a strict invariant: each node's list contains the highest-weighted words that descend from that node. We prove that insertion and query operations run in $O(\log N)$ time, where $N$ is the number of distinct words, and that the invariant is maintained after each update. Static abstract-syntax-tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 117 SLOC and 19 function blocks. The implementation is available in Swift on GitHub: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/swift-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261110_020122_design_typeahead_search_step_b}.
